hook: The Tian'e Longtan Bridge spans 600 meters, making it the world's longest concrete arch bridge.

sections.voiceover: The Tian'e Longtan Bridge spans 600 meters, making it the world's longest concrete arch bridge.
sections.visual_cue: Wide aerial shot of the massive concrete arch bridge spanning a deep reservoir.

sections.voiceover: Located in Tian'e County, China, this structure rises above the Longtan Reservoir. How much concrete fills these massive twin-ribbed arches?
sections.visual_cue: Map showing Guangxi, China, zooming into the bridge site, followed by a schematic of the twin-ribbed arch structure.

sections.voiceover: Constructing these ribs required a precise, ring-wise casting method to manage the weight.
sections.visual_cue: Close-up animation showing the segmented ring-wise casting process on the arch.

sections.voiceover: The final structure contains 27,944 cubic meters of external concrete. It stands as a feat of modern bridge engineering.
sections.visual_cue: Graphic displaying the concrete volume figure alongside the 125-meter rise measurement.

sections.voiceover: The bridge's clear span remains a record-breaking 600 meters.
sections.visual_cue: Final shot of the bridge reflecting on the water, highlighting the 600-meter span.
